questions.q:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements.

Statements:

All computers are laptops.

All hard disks are pen drives.

No pen drive is a keyboard.

No computer is a hard disk.

Conclusions:

I. Some pen drives are not laptops.

II. No keyboard is a computer.

III. No hard disk is a laptop.

IV. All pen drives are not keyboards.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is:



Conclusions:

I. Some pen drives are not laptops → False (because all pen drives can be laptops as there is no direct relationship between these two)

II. No keyboard is a computer → False (it is possible as shown but is not definite as there is no direct relation)

III. No hard disk is a laptop → False (because all hard disks can be laptop as there is no direct relationship between these two)

IV. All pen drives are not keyboards → True (as no pen drive is keyboard implies all pen drives are not keyboards)

Hence, only conclusion IV follows.

Additional Information

questions.q: In which of the following years was the origin and enactment of the Indian Age of Consent Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1891.

Key Points

• The Indian Age of Consent Act was legislation enacted in British India on 19 March 1891 that raised the age of consent for sexual intercourse from ten to twelve years for all girls in all jurisdictions.

• The Act was also known as Act X of 1891.

• It was an amendment to the Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, Section 375, 1882.

• Parishad member Sir Romesh Chunder Mitter (from Bengal) opposed it on the grounds that it interfered with the orthodox Hindu code.

• However, it received support from Indian reformers such as Behramji Malabari and women's social organizations.

questions.q: Which of the following is a private good?
options: A good that is consumed by a single person or household
A good that is available to everyone to consume, regardless of who pays for it and who does not.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A good that is consumed by a single person or household.

Key Points

• A good that is consumed by a single person or household is a private good.

• A public good is a product that one individual can consume without reducing its availability to others and from which no one is excluded.

• A private good is the opposite of a public good.

• A private good is a product that must be purchased to be consumed, and consumption by one individual prevents another individual from consuming it.

• We encounter private goods every day. For example- dinner at a restaurant, grocery shopping, airplane rides, and cellphones.

• Any item that is effectively destroyed or rendered unusable for its original purpose through use, such as food and toilet paper, are also private good.

questions.q: Of the known elements in the periodic table, only _ are gases under normal atmospheric conditions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 11.

Key Points

• Of the known elements in the periodic table, only 11 are gases under normal atmospheric conditions.

• These gases are hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, chlorine, helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.

• The periodic table is managed by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, or IUPAC.

• The modern periodic table sorts the elements according to increasing atomic number instead of increasing atomic mass.

• There are 118 elements in a periodic table.

• There are seven periods and eighteen groups in the modern periodic table.

Additional Information

• The size of the atoms (atomic size) decreases as we move from left to right in a period.

• The metallic properties of elements decrease while the non-metallic properties increase as we move from left to right in a period.

• Atoms increase in size (or increase in atomic size) as you move down a group of the periodic table.

• The metallic properties of elements increase as we move down the group of the periodic table.

questions.q: _ is a branch of biology that studies fungi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mycology.

Key Points

• Mycology is a branch of biology that studies fungi.

• Fungi are unicellular or multicellular thick-cell-walled heterotroph decomposers that eat decaying matter and form tangles of fibers.

• They use complex organic compounds as a source of energy and carbon, not photosynthesis.

• They are found in almost any habitat, but live mostly on land, primarily on soil or plant material rather than in sea or freshwater.

• A small number of fungi cause diseases in animals.

• In humans, fungal diseases include skin diseases such as athlete's foot, ringworm, and thrush.

Additional Information

• Morphology is the branch of biology that deals with the form of living organisms, and with relationships between their structures.

• Kalology is the branch of philosophy dealing with taste and the study of beauty in nature and art.

• Virology is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the biology of viruses and viral diseases.

questions.q: _ is a practice of establishing and managing individual trees generally for amenity purposes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arboriculture.

• Arboriculture is a practice of establishing and managing individual trees generally for amenity purposes.

Key Points

• The practice includes-

• propagating

• transplanting

• pruning

• applying fertilizer

• spraying to control insects and diseases

• cabling and bracing

• treating cavities

• identifying plants

• diagnosing and treating tree damage and ailments

• arranging plantings for their ornamental values

• removing trees

• The well-being of individual plants is the major concern of arboriculture.

• The science of arboriculture studies how these plants grow and respond to cultural practices and to their environment.

Additional Information

• Floriculture is a discipline of horticulture concerned with the growing and marketing of flowers and ornamental plants, in addition to, usage in floral arrangement and design.

• Viniculture is the cultivation and harvesting of grapes, primarily to make wine.

• Silviculture is the art and science of controlling the establishment, growth, composition, health, and quality of forests and woodlands. This is done to meet the diverse needs and values of landowners and society such as wildlife habitat, timber, water resources, restoration, and recreation on a sustainable basis.

• Gallium is a metallic material found as a trace element in coal, bauxite and other minerals.

• The symbol for gallium is "Ga" - (atomic number 31).

• The specialty semiconductors used for LED manufacturing are gallium arsenide (GaAs), gallium phosphide (GaP), or gallium arsenide phosphide (GaAsP).

Additional Information

• Indium gallium nitride (InGaN): blue, green and ultraviolet high-brightness LEDs

• Aluminum gallium indium phosphide (AlGaInP): yellow, orange and red high-brightness LEDs

• Aluminum gallium arsenide (AlGaAs): red and infrared LEDs

questions.q: The elements of the groups 3 to 12 are called _ elements or transition elements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is d-block.

Key Points

• Elements from groups 3 to 12 are called d-block elements or transition elements.

• As a group, they exhibit typical metallic properties and are less reactive than metals in groups 1 and 2.

• The term 'transition' refers to the fact that the d sublevel, which is in the process of filling, is at a lower principal energy level than the s sublevel previously filled.

• The electrons of transition metals can participate in the formation of chemical bonds - in two shells instead of just one.

• Transition metal compounds that dissolve in water exhibit a wide variety of bright colors.

• As visible light passes through a transition metal compound dissolved in water, the d-orbitals absorb light of different energies.

• Visible light of a given energy level that is not absorbed produces a solution of a specific colour.

Additional Information

• The periodic table is managed by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, or IUPAC.

• The modern periodic table sorts the elements according to increasing atomic number instead of increasing atomic mass.

• There are 118 elements in a periodic table.

• There are seven periods and eighteen groups in the modern periodic table.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

“Would you liked / to have / some fries / along with your coffee, / sir?” / asked the waiter.
questions.solution:
Method:
1. Identify the modal verb used in the sentence.
2. Check the verb form following the modal verb.
3. Apply the rule: Modal Verb + Base Form (V1).

Explanation:
The sentence uses the modal verb 'Would'. In English grammar, a modal verb (such as would, could, should, can, may) must always be followed by the base form of the verb (V1) without any 's', 'ed', or 'ing' endings. Therefore, 'liked' (V2/V3) is grammatically incorrect and must be replaced by 'like' (V1).

Why the others are wrong:
(B) some fries is correct as 'fries' is the plural noun for fried potatoes.
(C) asked the waiter is a correct reporting clause in the past tense.
(D) along with your coffee is a correct prepositional phrase.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The postman had delayed the letter.
options: The postman had been delayed by the letter.
The letter was delayed by the postman.
The letter had been delayed by the postman.
The letter had delayed the postman.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is The letter had been delayed by the postman.

Key Points

• The above-given sentence is in the active voice.

• We need to change it into passive voice.

• For converting the active voice into passive voice, the following steps should be taken:-

• The subject 'the postman' of the active voice becomes the object of the passive voice.

• The object 'the letter' of the active voice becomes the subject of the passive voice.

• The tense(past perfect tense) changes according to the following structure:-

• Active Voice - Subject + had + V3 + Object.

• Passive Voice - Object + had + been + V3 + Subject.

• Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.

Hinglish

• ऊपर दिया गया वाक्य Active voice में है ।

• हमें इसे passive voice में बदलने की जरूरत है।

• Active voice को passive voice में परिवर्तित करने के लिए, निम्नलिखित कदम उठाए जाने चाहिए: -

• Active voice का subject 'the postman' passive voice का object बन जाता है।

• Active voice का ऑब्जेक्ट 'the letter' passive voice का subject बन जाता है।

• निम्नलिखित संरचना के अनुसार काल (past perfect tense) बदल जाता है:-

• Active Voice - Subject + had + V3 + Object.

• Passive Voice - Object + had + been + V3 + Subject.

• अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।
